mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.50% q-o-q over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening in monetary and price stability policy, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both proxies exceed their 12-month averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for six consecutive months signals an extremely tight labor market, which elevates wage inflation and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to margin compression.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of persistently low unemployment (<3.5% for 6 months).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 1 million units for eight consecutive months signals a deepening housing market contraction, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.
